plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a classic winter bloomer in gardens across Japan, the southeastern United States, and Europe's Atlantic coast.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring, peaking January to March
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern US, UK, Portugal, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Thousands of cultivars exist, and the camellia is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree producing fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, often while snow is still on the ground. It is a beloved symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture.
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated in Japan, Korea, and Taiwan, and in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms appear weeks before cherry blossoms, and in Japan ume viewing parties are a long-standing tradition that predates hanami.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping white bell-shaped flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through frost and snow, carpeting woodlands and gardens in late winter.
plants.location: Native to Europe from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK, North America, and temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound used in medicine to treat symptoms of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: Large spreading tree with fern-like leaves and an umbrella-shaped crown. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, it is covered with brilliant clusters of flowers, followed by long woody seed pods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in the tropics in the dry season
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, Brazil, South Africa, and tropical regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite being widely planted across the tropics, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar.
